A promoted proposal must not exceed the queue-expiry time boundary.
A proposal cannot be promoted into the dequeued array without previously receiving upvotes.
Recorded referendum proposal IDs must agree with the votedFor tracking ghost whenever the proposal exists.
Dequeued entries must not reference proposal IDs beyond the proposal counter.
Upvote-record changes must preserve the encoded record-structure invariant.
A second upvote from a previously upvoting account must not increase that proposal's upvote total.
Successful proposal creation must increment proposalCount, while other successful actions must not decrease it.
No initial referendum vote totals may become positive unless the proposal was already approved.
Voting with the special None option cannot change a previous vote record or weight.

Ghost-recorded referendum proposal IDs must not exceed the proposal counter.
New approval requires dequeued presence and the documented approver identity.
Approval must not result in nonexistent proposals or be reversed while a proposal still exists.
Execution must not succeed when NO votes are at least YES votes.
The rule tests unauthorized mutation by method selector, excluding the known duration setters and initializer; it does not restrict msg.sender and cannot by itself prove a caller-authorization flaw.
Other operations may not increase queue length; the rule intentionally exempts propose.

Only initialize may change the initialized bit.

A second vote must not improperly alter a record or change multiple vote categories.
The sum of yes, no and abstain proposal votes must never exceed locked-gold voting weight.
The active property ends with assert true, so it cannot detect an illegal constitution change despite its name/comment.
The total nonvoting locked-gold balance must not be smaller than any one account's nonvoting balance.
For a self-initiated operation, the sum of available balance, nonvoting locked gold and pending withdrawals is conserved, subject to explicit selector and queue-length restrictions.
A transaction made by a different account must not change another account's nonvoting balance or pending withdrawals; the source handles withdraw differently.
Withdrawing a pending amount must increase the receiver's balance by that entry's value; the rule is also a prover-model diagnostic.
Before the unlocking period has elapsed, newly unlocked funds must remain in the account's locked or pending balances.

A caller already validating must not succeed in delegating validation.
A caller already voting must not successfully delegate voting.
